announcements.name: Expanded Windows ML and two new local models
announcements.shortDescription: Aion Instruct (an efficient reasoning SLM) and Aion Plan (a local agentic planning loop) run inbox on Windows across the full GPU install base, enabling onboard agents without cloud round trips.
announcements.longDescription: Microsoft is expanding the scope of Windows ML and Windows AI so developers can build local onboard AI that runs across the full install base of GPUs without round-tripping to the cloud. Two new models will run inbox on Windows: Aion Instruct, an efficient reasoning SLM, and Aion Plan, a planning model that provides a full local agentic loop. With tool access, developers can build fully onboard agentic applications. The expansion builds on existing local AI uses like Outlook Summarize, PowerPoint alt text, and third-party apps such as Adobe After Effects and Premiere using Windows ML across NPUs and GPUs.

announcements.name: Surface RTX Spark Dev Box
announcements.shortDescription: A developer "dream machine" with one petaflop of AI compute, 20 CPU cores, and 128 GB unified memory, available on a waitlist in the fall; Windows is also coming to NVIDIA's DGX station [inferred].
announcements.longDescription: Microsoft announced the Surface RTX Spark Dev Box, a developer "dream machine" that maxes out compute and memory on the new architecture. It delivers one petaflop of AI compute, 20 CPU cores, and 128 GB of unified memory access. It is coming in the fall, and attendees can join a waitlist. This follows the earlier Surface Ultra device that pairs NVIDIA power with Surface design, featuring 128 GB unified memory, a 2,000-nit display, and all-day battery life.

announcements.name: Windows developer experience updates
announcements.shortDescription: Intelligent Terminal with GitHub Copilot, 75+ Linux command-line utilities (grep, curl, tar, sudo), Homebrew/Starship/Zsh support, vertical taskbar, and first-class WSL containers.
announcements.longDescription: Microsoft announced a range of Windows developer experience updates aimed at making Windows the best place to build, whether on laptop, desktop, or cloud. These include a distraction-free dev environment, an intelligent terminal with built-in GitHub Copilot, and extensive Linux support with 70-plus command-line utilities (such as grep) now available on Windows. It also brings Mac-loved tools like Starship, Z Shell, and native Homebrew, and introduces first-class WSL containers to ease environment management. Windows 365 also gains a developer distribution optimized for cloud productivity.

announcements.name: Azure infrastructure at scale
announcements.shortDescription: 500+ data centers across 80 regions; the Fairwater AI super-factory (Georgia and Wisconsin) runs near-zero-water cooling and the largest Grace Blackwell deployment; Maia 200 (live in Iowa and Arizona) delivers 30% better tokens per dollar; Cobalt 200 VMs enter preview.
announcements.longDescription: Satya Nadella detailed Azure's infrastructure scale, noting it now spans more than 500 data centers across 80 regions—the most expansive hyperscaler footprint—with more capacity added in the last 18 months than in Azure's first decade. He emphasized end-to-end systems optimization from electrons to tokens and community-grounded principles like not raising electricity prices and replenishing water use. He highlighted Fairwater, the first AI super-factory spanning Georgia and Wisconsin, designed from the ground up for AI in close collaboration with NVIDIA, using a two-story architecture to densely pack GPUs. The transcript window does not detail Maia 200 or Cobalt 200 specifics.

announcements.name: Horizon DB
announcements.shortDescription: A fully managed, zone-redundant PostgreSQL service with 128 TB per cluster, 15 read replicas, and ~3x throughput over self-managed Postgres.
announcements.longDescription: Microsoft announced Horizon DB, a fully managed PostgreSQL service on Azure built ground-up for high-availability scale-out. It is zone-redundant with automated failover, offers 128 terabytes of storage per cluster, and supports 15 read replicas to scale read-heavy workloads. In internal testing, Horizon delivers roughly 3x throughput compared to any self-managed PostgreSQL setup. It is positioned to support the data-tier needs of agentic systems that continuously store, retrieve, reason, act, and learn.

announcements.name: Web IQ and Microsoft IQ
announcements.shortDescription: Model-agnostic, MCP-native web grounding plus a unified IQ layer (Web IQ, Fabric IQ, Work IQ, Foundry IQ) for grounding agents in enterprise context.
announcements.longDescription: Microsoft announced Web IQ, a web-grounding capability built on its global infrastructure serving over a billion users but re-architected for LLM and agentic workflows. It is model-agnostic and MCP-native, plugs into any agent runtime, and spans web, news, images, and video so agents can ground responses in fresh, verifiable content, leading in quality, speed, and cost. Above the data tier, Microsoft is building a unified IQ layer that brings together Foundry, Fabric, and Microsoft 365 for a continuously updated understanding of an organization. This structured context aims to deliver the right grounding to make models more token-efficient.

announcements.name: Microsoft Execution Containers (MXC)
announcements.shortDescription: OS-native isolation/containment policy for agents; OpenClaw runs natively on Windows via MXC with a WinUI 3 companion app.
announcements.longDescription: Microsoft introduced Microsoft Execution Containers (MXC), a new policy layer that lets Windows apply isolation and containment to agents using OS-native primitives baked into the operating system so containment is enforced by policy. Options range from process-level isolation for lightweight agent actions, session-level isolation for user separation, Windows and Linux VMs (including WSL) for stronger boundaries, to Windows 365 for agents for maximum isolation in a separate managed environment. Developers can pick the right containment option per workload and Windows enforces it via MXC, regardless of who built the agent. NVIDIA is bringing OpenClaw [inferred] to Windows to securely execute autonomous AI agents.

announcements.name: GitHub Copilot app and Rayfin SDK
announcements.shortDescription: A new app managing parallel agent sessions via git worktrees, with Rayfin providing an enterprise backend-as-a-service (partnered with Replit, hosted on Microsoft Fabric).
announcements.longDescription: Microsoft introduced a new GitHub Copilot app that combines the speed and flexibility of a CLI with the capability of an IDE and the ability to scale to an effectively infinite number of agent sessions, addressing the cognitive overload of managing many CLI sessions. Alongside it, Microsoft announced Rayfin [inferred], an agent-first SDK that connects agents to a backend-as-a-service, handling identities, storage, and database schemas. In partnership with Replit, developers can build apps in Replit while the app and data deploy into an enterprise-managed Fabric tenant via the Rayfin SDK. The Rayfin SDK is available now for use with other tools as a backend service.

announcements.name: Agent 365 and MDASH
announcements.shortDescription: Agent control plane (Entra, Defender, Purview extensions) with Agent 365 SDK GA, plus MDASH, a 100+ agent security harness that topped the CyberGym benchmark.
announcements.longDescription: Microsoft Agent 365 provides governance so every agent in an organization is managed with the same rigor as users, apps, and devices, letting admins review details, control who can talk to an agent, and monitor or block it at any time even after approval. Microsoft also highlighted MDASH, its multi-model agentic security system announced the prior month—an agent harness for security that brings together over 100 agents across frontier and custom models to find exploitable bugs better than any single model. When debuted, the harness topped the CyberGym benchmark. It runs as a standalone CLI (also usable in the GitHub Copilot app), breaks results down by vulnerability domain and severity, identifies AI-specific vulnerabilities, and generates SARIF logs and HTML reports.

announcements.name: Autopilots and Scout
announcements.shortDescription: Enterprise-grade autonomous agents with identity and compliance; Scout is the first, available on Copilot Frontier.
announcements.longDescription: Microsoft introduced Autopilots, described as enterprise-grade autonomous, long-running agents with full enterprise compliance that run in your tenant. Autopilots can have a name, personality, custom connectors, context, and memory, offering a new way to reduce toil. They join the evolving Copilot experience of Chat, Cowork, and Code converging into one Copilot super app. The first autopilot being introduced is Scout.

announcements.name: Seven new MAI models and Frontier Tuning
announcements.shortDescription: MAI Image-2.5, Transcribe-1.5, Voice-2, Thinking-1, and Code-1-Flash, with a Mayo Clinic partnership to co-develop a healthcare frontier model.
announcements.longDescription: MAI announced a family of seven new models spanning Image, Voice, Transcription, and Coding, tuned for practical, efficient real-world use. MAI Image-2.5 and its Flash variant deliver a step change in quality, reaching number two on the leaderboard and surpassing Nano Banana 2 on image editing; they are live in PowerPoint, rolling out to OneDrive, and available on Foundry. MAI Transcribe-1.5 is positioned as the best transcription model in the world with state-of-the-art accuracy across 43 languages, beating Gemini and OpenAI flagship models and running five times faster, integrated into GitHub, Teams, and Copilot. The announcement frames these within MAI's pursuit of humanist superintelligence.

announcements.name: Majorana 2
announcements.shortDescription: Next-generation topological qubit with a 20-second-to-one-minute mean lifetime (~1,000x Majorana 1) and one-microsecond operations.
announcements.longDescription: Satya Nadella announced Majorana 2, the next-generation topological qubit implementing a new material stack discovered, built, and fabricated with the help of Microsoft's discovery agentic loop. Its qubits are exceptionally reliable, providing a mean lifetime of 20 seconds up to a minute—about a thousand times higher than Majorana 1—while operations run in one microsecond, enabling complex quantum computation within that lifetime. It retains the same qubit form factor as Majorana 1 at one one-hundredth of a millimeter, controlled all digitally, making it possible to fit a million qubits on a chip smaller than a credit card. With Majorana 1 having proven the foundational physics, Majorana 2 begins the engineering scale phase.
